records.native_title: Love the product, hate the packaging
records.native_body: I do actually love this product across the board. The problem is with the packaging. The lid keeps coming unscrewed and tonight it came loose in my pocket at work so it seeped onto my brand new underwear, and also onto my work shirt and of course there’s now a spot on my jeans. Worse, once I collected all the loose product onto my pinkie I had no way to put it back into the package. I hate complaining about packaging because that’s not made in house. That’s ordered from a manufacturer, so. I don’t know if maybe it should do a whole click lock when you screw the cap on, or if a doe foot option might be worth it? I just hate that because void is my favorite I’ve lost a lot of it to the lid coming off so I will repurchase. I love it so so much, but I’m very annoyed to lose so much product when it’s not that cheap.

records.native_title: Love the product, hate the packaging
records.native_body: I do actually love this product across the board. The problem is with the packaging. The lid keeps coming unscrewed and tonight it came loose in my pocket at work so it seeped onto my brand new underwear, and also onto my work shirt and of course there’s now a spot on my jeans. Worse, once I collected all the loose product onto my pinkie I had no way to put it back into the package. I hate complaining about packaging because that’s not made in house. That’s ordered from a manufacturer, so. I don’t know if maybe it should do a whole click lock when you screw the cap on, or if a doe foot option might be worth it? I just hate that because void is my favorite I’ve lost a lot of it to the lid coming off so I will repurchase. I love it so so much, but I’m very annoyed to lose so much product when it’s not that cheap.

answer.report:
Across the complete supplied source set: Packaging attracts praise for appearance, refillability and perceived environmental merit. P00’s chic/environmentally friendly statement has 296 displayed likes; P15’s intended empty-container reuse has 150. These show resonance with those statements, not verified sustainability, reuse or purchasing effects. Several distinct accounts praise packaging, but share one brand-owned TikTok thread. P02 questions recyclability; P03’s qualified answer is from P00’s own author, and P01 is brand agreement. Environmental performance remains unverified. P26 praises packaging while asking what the product does for skin.

P06 reports arrival leakage with a loose top, cleanup and concern about oxygen exposure. P07 offers a replacement and says short exposure is not an issue; this is brand reassurance, not independent evidence of product integrity or completed remedy.

Seven distinct focal TikTok accounts report or contextually agree to arrival leakage: P06, P08–P13. Three provide more than bare agreement: P06 describes the loose top and cleanup; P08 adds Sephora ordering and a free replacement reportedly sent; P13 describes an improperly screwed top and major leak after ordering from Sephora. Four are terse agreements. Thus arrival leakage has distinct-account recurrence within one reply branch, with unequal detail; only P06 and P13 independently describe a loose/improperly screwed top. Their raw likes are respectively 12 and 0; P08 has 5, and bare agreements have 4, 4, 2 and 0. Zero likes do not negate testimony. These are account counts, not verified independent-human or event counts. Complaint SKU/version remains unknown, and agreement cannot supply every detail of P06’s experience.

R01 separately reports Softwear–Void’s lid repeatedly unscrewing during use, including leakage in a work pocket, stained clothing and unrecoverable product. This adds retailer-review evidence of leakage and closure problems at a broader level, but does not corroborate arrival failure for the unidentified TikTok product. It is one account reporting recurrence, not a count of separately established incidents. Its proposed click-lock or doe-foot changes are suggestions, not implemented remedies.

Consequences: P07 offers service replacement; P08 reports Sephora sent one free, without delivery confirmation. R01 explicitly intends to repurchase because Void is a favorite despite product loss, expense and strong packaging dissatisfaction; the review is 3/5 and recommends the product. P17 reports an all-Experiment routine and Continuum in transit, but attributes neither to packaging. P20 expresses broad buying enthusiasm without confirming completed purchases. P32 may save up; P38 wants to try; P42 reports receipt and only then discovering refillability, so that discovery cannot explain the already-completed acquisition. P04/P27 request refill bundles, P29 asks about a refill sticker, and P15 proposes reuse; these do not establish repeat purchases.

Reception is mixed across dimensions: aesthetic/refill enthusiasm coexists with functional complaints and complaint alongside loyalty. There is no direct rebuttal of the specific leak reports, but no basis for a general defect rate, failure mechanism, safety conclusion or packaging-driven buying effect. General praise does not establish leak-free use. Product/formula versions are unavailable; named Continuum/Super Saturated requests and Softwear–Void testimony must not assign those products to unspecified comments. No joint-use evidence resolves complaint scope.
